requirements.FR-01: Users can submit lost and found reports; the server validates every field (type, category, text length, real calendar date within the allowed window).
requirements.FR-02: Duplicate reports by the same reporter are rejected, without falsely rejecting different items.
requirements.FR-03: Lost and found reports are matched automatically into candidate matches using category, description, location and date.
requirements.FR-04: Candidate-match notifications are delivered with bounded retries, backoff and recovery; permanent failures are routed to staff.
requirements.FR-05: Ownership is verified manually and release follows a strict state machine that cannot hand an item over twice or skip verification.
requirements.FR-06: Unclaimed found items trigger one aging reminder (30 days) and one disposal review (90 days).
requirements.FR-07: Staff handle failed notifications and disposal reviews through a manual queue (re-send, resolve, dispose).
requirements.FR-08: Every state change is audited and system events are logged in structured form.
requirements.SR-01: Users authenticate with credentials; sessions use signed, expiring, revocable tokens; brute force is limited.
requirements.SR-02: Access is authorised on the server by role and by object ownership.
requirements.SR-03: Data is protected in transit (HTTPS) and responses carry security headers; CORS is restricted.
requirements.SR-04: Secrets and environment settings are protected; production fails fast on unsafe configuration.
requirements.SR-05: All input is validated and malformed or hostile input is rejected safely.
requirements.SR-06: Logs never contain credentials, tokens or report text.
requirements.SR-07: API responses expose only the data each role needs.
requirements.NF-01: The system is reliable: errors are generic, state stays consistent, writes are atomic and concurrency is safe.
requirements.NF-02: The API interoperates with standard clients: content types, CORS preflight, authorization scheme case, Unicode text.
requirements.NF-03: Resource use is bounded: rate limits, body size, paging, in-memory tracking tables.
requirements.UI-01: Sign-in and session handling in the Flutter app, including failure, lockout and expiry states.
requirements.UI-02: Report submission shows validation, loading, success, duplicate and error states.
requirements.UI-03: Match review and manual queue controls are role-appropriate and update the list after each action.
requirements.UI-04: Every list or screen has loading, empty, network, authorization and server-error states with correct retry behaviour.
requirements.UI-05: The layout adapts between phone and desktop widths.
requirements.NF-04: Operability: liveness and readiness probes, staff-only metrics (latency percentiles, errors, process and event-loop health) and slow-request logging allow problems to be detected.
requirements.NF-05: Performance and capacity: stated response-time and error targets are met under ordinary and peak load, and the cost of a request does not grow with the amount of stored data.
requirements.NF-06: Recoverability: acknowledged writes survive crashes, shutdown is graceful, corrupt storage recovers from backup, and a bad release can be rolled back.
requirements.UI-06: Staff can see both items side by side when deciding a match and must record the proof checked or the reason for refusing; irreversible steps ask for confirmation.
requirements.UI-07: Users see plain-language messages (status, notifications, confirmations) instead of internal ids and codes, and messages stay visible long enough to read.
requirements.UI-08: Production builds expose no developer or demonstration tools.
requirements.FR-09: Matching precision: generic shared words do not create candidates, while brief lost descriptions still match detailed found items.
requirements.DOC-01: The API is documented in OpenAPI 3 and the document is exactly accurate: same routes, response codes, schemas, security and roles as the running server.
requirements.DEP-01: The static host serves the Flutter app compressed, always revalidates non-fingerprinted files (no stale app code after a deploy) and sends baseline security headers.
